html:
Lobengula was the second and last king of the Ndebele, ruling from Bulawayo from 1868 until his kingdom was conquered in 1893.

The son of Mzilikazi, he tried to hold off the many Europeans seeking gold and land by granting limited favours and playing them against each other. The Rudd Concession he signed in 1888 was used by Cecil Rhodes to take over his lands.

In 1893 the British South Africa Company provoked a war, and its troops with machine guns defeated the Ndebele regiments. Lobengula burned his capital and fled north, and died in about early 1894. His kingdom became part of Rhodesia, and the Ndebele rose again in the rising of 1896.
